name: Sulfathiazole

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in United States and 2 other countries, first in 1970 — for kidney harm, liver harm and serious skin reactions

summary: Sulfathiazole was taken off the market in the United States and two other countries starting in 1970 due to kidney damage, liver damage, and severe skin reactions [3]. Based on a small computer model rather than human tests, it received a high risk score of 93 for the liver and a low risk score of 16 for the heart [M]. Additionally, a similar drug called Sulfamethazine was pulled from the German market in 1992 [4]. Another related drug, Sulfacarbamide, was also removed from the market in Germany in 1988 because of liver harm and blood disorders [5].
